title: Emission fingerprint decomposition for per-token cost and cache signal
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: We need high-fidelity, token-level attribution signals that explain latency and cost per emitted token while accounting for KV cache behavior (hits vs misses) without adding significant runtime overhead. Existing coarse-grained traces hide inter-token variance and make billing reconciliations and regression detection noisy.

Goal: Produce a lightweight, production-safe "emission fingerprint" for every response that decomposes per-token time contributions (scheduling, kernel execution, batching overhead, and KV lookup cost) and marks whether each token benefited from a KV cache hit. These fingerprints should feed both the tracing system and the metrics/log pipeline so dashboards and billing reconciliation can perform accurate attribution and root-cause analysis.

High-level approach: Instrument four low-cost anchors in the serving runtime: pre-emit marker (token index), kernel-start, kernel-end, and kv-lookup result. Rather than instrumenting with full-span objects per token (expensive), we will inject compact, fixed-width markers into an off-path aggregation buffer. Markers are sampled at configurable rates and always include: request_id, model, route, token_index, micro-timestamp deltas (kernel and kv), and kv_hit boolean. Sampling is complemented by a deterministic compensation algorithm that upweights sampled data to estimate per-token totals for billing and SLA attribution. Aggregates are exported asynchronously to the tracing/metric pipeline in batches to avoid synchronous overhead.

Requirements:
- Max added p99 latency <= 3% for non-sampled requests and <= 10% for sampled tail cases under normal load.
- Sampling default 1% with configurable burst-smoothing for short high-QPS spikes.
- KV-hit attribution must be explicit per-token to allow delta-between-hit-and-miss estimation.
- Export pipeline must preserve request metadata (customer id, route, model_version) but strip any PII in accordance with privacy policy.
- Backcompat: if emission fingerprinting is disabled or unsupported on an old runtime, logs must still include coarse per-request timing to avoid data gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Emission fingerprints emitted for sampled requests and persisted to observability pipeline
KV-hit flag appears on per-token records and aligns with cache telemetry (>98% agreement in synthetic tests)
End-to-end ingestion shows token-attribution metrics in dashboards (per-route p50/p95/p99 breakdown by token index)
Overhead validated in staging: <3% p99 latency for typical non-sampled traffic; sampling path measured and documented
Billing reconciliation test demonstrates cache-adjusted per-token costing within 1.5% of ground-truth simulation
implementation_plan: Design: finalize compact marker schema (fixed-width binary + protobuf preview); decide fields to include to balance signal vs overhead
Runtime: add three lightweight hooks: emit_marker(), record_kernel_bounds(), record_kv_outcome(); implement off-path ring buffer and async exporter
Sampling: implement deterministic hashing per request for stable sampling; add burst-smoothing algorithm to avoid correlated sampling under high QPS
Aggregation: server-side aggregator rolls up sampled markers into compact mini-batches tagged with time windows and publishes to the observability pipeline (Kafka/OTLP)
Pipeline: add parser to metrics/log pipeline to expand markers into token-level events and attach to trace spans; produce derived metrics for dashboards
Dashboards/Alerts: build per-route dashboards showing per-token latency slices, cache-hit delta curves, and alerts for regression thresholds
Tests: synthetic workload to validate overhead, correctness test for kv-hit alignment, billing reconciliation harness to validate compensation model
Rollout: enable in canary mode on 10% of hosts, monitor overhead and signal fidelity for 1 week, ramp to 100% if green
tradeoffs: Full per-token spans would be most accurate but are too expensive at scale; sampling + compensation trades some fidelity for tractability
Including more fields (full token text or ids) improves debugging but raises privacy and overhead concerns; we explicitly exclude token text from exported markers
Synchronous exports simplify correctness but add latency; we choose async, batched export with an in-memory buffer and backpressure safeguards
dashboards: Observability > Token Attribution > Per-route token latency waterfall (p50/p95/p99)
Observability > Token Attribution > KV hit delta (avg latency saved per-hit by token index)
Billing > Token Cost Reconciliation > Estimated vs actual (rolling 24h)
SRE > Infra Overhead > Emission fingerprint export lag and buffer saturation
